prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1232; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Nothing independent confirms the accident: no witnesses, no photos and no other report.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured's policy-named driver reported a hit while turning left at an intersection. The claimant states the other vehicle pulled out of a side street and struck the rear passenger side of the claimant's car.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that the vehicle is listed under this coverage. Assigned the file for a standard review of liability and injury.

Entry 3: Police records and the officer's notes place the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of the collision. No independent witness statements have been obtained to date, and no photographs of the scene have been received from any source.

Entry 4: Spoke with the claimant by phone. The account matched the first call word for word, including the direction of travel and the position of the other car.

Entry 5: Reviewed the damage estimate. The rear quarter panel, bumper bracket and rear wheel well damage is mostly consistent with the impact described in the statement.

Entry 6: A few older scratches appear along the lower left door. These may predate this incident, and I have noted them separately so they are not added to the current repair scope without verification.

Entry 7: Received the claimant's report of a back strain. The reported symptoms are plausible for a side impact of this kind and the initial treatment plan is reasonable.

Entry 8: Checked prior claims and medical history. No earlier injury to the same area of the back is on record, and no previous claim involving this vehicle's body area has been found.

Entry 9: A neighbor contacted the office and believes the car already had body damage some weeks before the date given by the claimant. The statement is unsigned and has not yet been verified.

Entry 10: Treatment has continued for somewhat longer than is typical for a strain of this type. The provider's notes explain the additional visits as part of a gradual recovery plan, and I have requested the full treatment records.

Entry 11: The claimant is not represented by an attorney and has been given the claims process information in writing. I have explained the next steps and the documents still needed.

Entry 12: File remains open pending the neighbor's account, the scratch assessment, and receipt of the complete treatment records. No coverage decision has been made.
